verdict.rationale: Stripe's security guide says its low-risk payment integrations collect and send payment information directly to Stripe without it passing through the merchant's servers, which reduces PCI obligations. Checkout (embedded or Stripe-hosted) and Elements are the documented integration surfaces for collecting payment details this way. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of the tokenization mechanism and of which PCI validation level (e.g., SAQ type) applies, plus independent or hands-on corroboration of the scope reduction.

support.subject: As a developer, I can keep my systems out of most of PCI DSS scope because card data is tokenized and never touches my servers

citations.quote: You can instead use one of our low risk payment integrations to securely collect and transmit payment information directly to Stripe without it passing through your servers, reducing your PCI obligations.
Customers enter their payment details in a fully-featured payment page, either embedded on your site or via a redirect to a Stripe-hosted page.
